title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Test Card Home — the TV's broadcast identity as its home screen's system. Keep it, take the pick or a competitive challenger, adopt a declined one, or re-roll.

options.label: Test Card Home
options.lineage: broadcast test cards and signal discipline (SMPTE/ITT-era TV identity)
options.thesis: The TV's own on-air identity, worn as its home screen.
options.viewport: One glanceable screen: tabular clock, favorites rail with icon badges, input rail, and a test-card signal strip along the bottom edge whose lit segment shows what is live; no panning, no hero line.
options.risk: Reads clinical if the strip, hairlines and micro-labels become ornament instead of state; every colour must mean something.

raised.raise: Unfocused tiles keep quiet — only the focused tile carries a state line.
Panels cut on a 90 ms two-frame step, never a long ease.
Clock and counts set as tabular numerals in fixed fields.
State stamps in place; rows never reorder when they change.
One grotesque at a strict scale, hairlines and letterspaced micro-labels only.
The grid is the armature: every tile and gutter snaps to one visible rhythm.

options.label: Hi-Fi Faceplate
options.thesis: The living room's dial era: apps as faceplate buttons, inputs as a selector scale.
options.viewport: Favorites as machined lit buttons; the input selector drawn as a labeled hairline scale with the live input under the pointer; clock in a recessed display window.
options.risk: Familiarity — this is the most-worn minimalism lane in industrial design.

options.label: Streaming Title-Card Wall
options.thesis: Everything as familiar shelves: the focused tile expands and reveals its metadata, the rest dims.
options.case: Holds audience familiarity; loses product clarity — this is the shelf-plus-pan arrangement the owner just rejected on this TV.
options.risk: Every smart TV ships this; indistinguishable from the incumbent.

options.label: Manual Tab Board
options.lineage: boxed-software reference manuals, tabbed section boards
options.thesis: A stepped tab rail carries the surfaces; each section owns one saturated hue; changes step, never ease.
options.case: Strong for an owner who lives by service manuals — but a tab board cannot carry the seconds-long glance home screen.
options.risk: Digs deep into settings navigation while the home glance needs to stay instant.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: A barcode lattice of hairline bars with dense monospace numbers.
options.case: Pure black-and-white purity forbids the live/standby colour semantics the product needs.
options.kept: Tabular numerals and fixed number fields.
options.risk: Costume of a concert hall, not a living room.

options.label: Jet-Age Ticket Wallet
options.lineage: carbon-copy travel coupons and baggage stubs
options.thesis: Each launch as a coupon torn from an official wallet.
options.case: Paper coupon costume fails at 3 m on an 85-inch panel.
options.kept: State stamps in place; records never reorder.

options.label: Design Annual Plates
options.lineage: print annual plate sections on uncoated stock
options.thesis: Near-white printed sheets with registration crosses and one grotesque.
options.case: A near-white ground glares from the couch at night on an 85-inch panel.
options.kept: One grotesque at a strict scale; hairline precision.

options.label: Crouwel Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Monumental grid-constructed letterforms on a visible construction grid.
options.case: Monumental letterforms are a poster; they displace the apps instead of serving them.
options.kept: The grid itself as the visible armature.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The shelf launcher visitors expect, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: A billboard for the last-watched item above, shelves of real apps and inputs below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
